chapter_theme: The rule of eating: devotees are welcomed and fed everywhere as if with nectar, and those who know the grace within Siva beg at noon for the Lord in the inner temple, eat without distinction and sit apart, free of desire.

1884.reading: In all eight directions people welcome the Lord's devotees with prepared food, calling it nectar; those who cling to ruling a piece of land would not know desire for it if they left it lying.
1884.nuance: கட்ட அடிசில் may be food made ready or food bundled for the road. The second half is obscure; it may contrast the devotee, fed everywhere, with the king who clings to his land, or say that a king who gave up his land for this life would not miss it.

1885.reading: Those who know the grace standing within Siva beg alms at noon for the Lord in the temple within, eat, think of all without distinction, give up desire and sit raised in solitude.
1885.nuance: உள்ளமர் கோவில் is the temple within, the heart where the Lord dwells, so the alms are begged for him and eating is an offering. பேதம் அற நினைந்து may mean without distinguishing donors or without the sense of self and other.

links.note: Both place the Lord in the devotee: 1857 tells the giver that food for the walking temple reaches the god, 1885 tells the devotee that he begs and eats for the Lord in the temple within.

1884 says people in all eight directions welcome the Lord's devotees with prepared food, calling it nectar. Kural 263 asks whether the others have forgotten tapas 'துறந்தார்க்குத் துப்புரவு வேண்டி', in wanting to provide for renouncers. Both describe the householder's role as feeding those who have renounced; the Kural adds a note of irony that the Tirumanthiram lacks.
